tip_title: Your Flood Policy Might Replace Your Stuff for Less Than It Costs to Buy It Again
topic: Flood Insurance - Contents Coverage and Replacement Cost Gap
blurb:
💡 **Insurance Tip: Your Flood Policy Might Replace Your Stuff for Less Than It Costs to Buy It Again**

If you have a flood policy through the National Flood Insurance Program, there's a detail about your contents coverage worth knowing: NFIP pays out on personal belongings based on actual cash value, which means depreciation gets factored in. A five-year-old couch isn't worth what a new couch costs, as far as the claim goes. Some private flood insurers offer replacement cost coverage on contents as an add-on — meaning you'd get closer to what it actually costs to replace the item today, not what it was worth before the flood. If you've had your flood policy for a while and never looked at how your contents would be paid out, this is a good week to ask.

Not sure how your current flood policy handles contents claims? Your Peachy agent can pull up the details and walk you through it.

📖 Learn more from the Insurance Information Institute (https://www.iii.org/article/spotlight-on-flood-insurance)
summary: Covers the actual cash value vs. replacement cost distinction for personal belongings under flood insurance, specifically that NFIP pays ACV on contents while some private flood policies offer replacement cost as an add-on — distinct from prior tips on the building/contents election and NFIP vs. private purchase decision.
